title: Rebalance three emergency kits without spares
instruction: Each grey mat is an emergency kit. Make each kit hold exactly one white mask, one yellow torch and one red dressing pack. There are no spares, so move items between the kits. Leave items that already belong where they are.
context: Every module of a station or lunar base keeps a complete emergency set, as every hospital ward keeps a crash cart and every vehicle a first-aid kit. Sets are checked against a fixed list, and after use or an audit they are rebalanced from one another when no stock is at hand. A set with two masks and no torch fails the check as surely as an empty one, and an item that already passed stays where the crew expect to find it. The test is closed, minimal redistribution: read each kit's surplus and gap and move only the surplus. Each kit holds one item twice and lacks another, and each surplus sits in a different kit, so no swap between two kits completes both, and the only end state that scores in full is the one a three-way cycle reaches. Filling a gap from the nearest item of its kind takes another kit's only one, which then has to go back. Unlike setting places or filling baskets from a pile, there is no pile: every item is already in a kit.
setup: Station table, in front of the left arm; the right arm is idle at its ready pose. Table coordinates in metres: x forward from the line through the two arm bases, y left from the midline, heights above the table top; the left arm's base is at y = +0.305. All objects are rigid and matte with one shared friction (1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic). Fixed, grey (sRGB 0.55, 0.55, 0.58): three identical kit mats, boards 240 x 90 x 3 mm (x, y, z) lying on the table, centred at x = 0.215 and y = 0.420 (kit 1), 0.300 (kit 2) and 0.180 (kit 3). Each spans x 0.095 to 0.335; in y, kit 1 spans 0.375 to 0.465, kit 2 0.255 to 0.345 and kit 3 0.135 to 0.225, with 30 mm of bare table between mats. Kit 1 is on the left as seen from behind the arms, which is also the left of the top camera image. The mats carry no labels or marked places. Loose, standing on the mats on each mat's centre line: masks, white (sRGB 0.92, 0.92, 0.92) boxes 40 x 50 x 35 mm (x, y, z), 40 g, lying on a 40 x 50 face; torches, yellow (sRGB 0.95, 0.80, 0.15) cylinders 30 mm in diameter and 60 mm tall, 50 g, standing on end; dressing packs, red (sRGB 0.80, 0.15, 0.15) boxes 45 x 50 x 25 mm, 30 g, lying on a 45 x 50 face. There are three of each, nine in all. At the start, at x = 0.125, 0.185 and 0.245 on each mat: kit 1 holds mask, mask, dressing; kit 2 holds torch, torch, mask; kit 3 holds dressing, dressing, torch. The place at x = 0.305 is free on every mat. So kit 1 lacks a torch, kit 2 a dressing and kit 3 a mask, and each surplus is in a different kit. Neighbours on a mat have 15 to 30 mm of air between them, items on neighbouring mats at least 70 mm, and nothing touches. Every item and free place is within 0.33 m of the left arm's base. To build it: cut three 240 x 90 mm boards from 3 mm sheet, paint them grey and tape them to the table at the stated centres; make the masks and dressing packs from foam or printed boxes and the torches from 30 mm rod or tube, weighted to the stated masses and painted; tape small marks for the start places on the mats' side edges, for reset and for measuring whether a kept item stayed within 15 mm.
scoring: End state only, judged after the arm has released and moved clear, from a top photo and a tape measure; in simulation on the final step. An item is over a mat when its centre lies inside that mat's 240 x 90 mm outline as seen from above and its lowest point is less than 100 mm above the mat top. An item over a mat is set down in that kit when it is at rest (under 10 mm/s and 0.5 rad/s) on a face or an end with its lowest point within 4 mm of the mat top: a box with one of its own axes within 10 degrees of vertical (any face, either way up), a torch with its axis within 10 degrees of vertical (on an end) or of horizontal (lying). A kit check reads contents, not pose. Any other item over a mat (still moving, leaning, tipped onto a corner or edge, on another item or more than 4 mm above the mat) spoils that kit. A kit is complete when nothing spoils it, the items set down in it are exactly one mask, one torch and one dressing pack, and the items it kept are in place: seen from above, its single item's centre within 15 mm of that item's start place, and the centre of the one item it keeps of its doubled kind within 15 mm of either start place that held that kind. Items of a kind are interchangeable. An item moved in may sit anywhere on its new mat, and a kept item may turn or tip where it stands. Items off every mat and items more than 100 mm above a mat count for no kit. Score = complete kits / 3: 0, 1/3, 2/3 or 1.0. Success, which ends the trial, is 1.0 held for 1 s. Reference outcomes: the start scores 0. The three cycle moves (kit 1's extra mask to kit 3, kit 3's extra dressing to kit 2, kit 2's extra torch to kit 1) score 1.0; any two of them complete one kit, 1/3; one alone, 0. Swapping two kits' surpluses completes only one, 1/3. Filling kit 3's gap from kit 2, the nearest kit with a mask, scores 0 at that point; each later move that completes a kit adds 1/3, and kit 2 counts again only once a mask is back on its mask place. Regrouping all nine one of each per mat moves items that belonged, so only kits whose kept items stayed count. Taking surpluses to the table, 0. A push or sweep completes a kit only by leaving the right three items in it with the kept ones in place, so sliding an item onto the next mat earns what carrying it would. Values exactly on a limit pass (0.1 mm margin). In simulation every test uses each item's centre and orientation, not its axis-aligned bounds, and the scorer cannot see the gripper, so an item held motionless over a mat is judged as if it rested there; on the real rig the photo after the arm withdraws decides. The mats are fixed in simulation; on the real rig a trial in which a mat moves more than 5 mm from its mark scores 0.
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed. Stand the nine items back on their start places: kit 1 mask, mask, dressing; kit 2 torch, torch, mask; kit 3 dressing, dressing, torch, at x = 0.125, 0.185 and 0.245, leaving x = 0.305 free on every mat. The mats do not move.
fidelity: Approximate: plain rigid stand-ins, a box for a mask pouch, a cylinder for a torch and a flatter box for a dressing pack, told apart by shape and colour, not labels. The kits are flat mats, not bags or drawers, so an item is in a kit by position. One shared friction (1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic), matte colours, Earth gravity on a bench, as for a ward's crash cart; aboard a station the same audit is done in microgravity, which is not modelled.
